claims.text: Local lattice distortions originating from short-range chemical ordering control strength and deformation behavior in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Short-range chemical ordering influences dislocation motion.
As-cast multi-component concentrated alloys exhibit inherent chemical heterogeneity.
As-cast multi-component concentrated alloys exhibit significant short-range order.
Elevated-temperature annealing followed by rapid quenching will reduce or homogenize short-range chemical order.
Short-range chemical ordering induces local lattice distortions.
Short-range chemical order creates local atomic misfits.
The local atomic misfits associated with short-range order act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by these local atomic misfits increases alloy strength.
Reducing short-range order diminishes the local atomic misfits.
Diminishing the local atomic misfits decreases yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples will have lower yield strength because local-lattice-distortion-mediated dislocation pinning is diminished.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples may exhibit increased ductility.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to multi-component alloys having significant atomic-size mismatch, chemical complexity, and appreciable short-range order.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to simpler substitutional solid solutions or alloys lacking appreciable short-range order.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property change depends on alloy-specific parameters and annealing conditions.
